context.title: Who Is My Neighbour?
context.summary: Jesus sends out seventy messengers, who return rejoicing. A lawyer's question leads to the parable of the good Samaritan, and in Martha's home Mary sits at Jesus' feet to listen.
context.background: Some manuscripts read seventy-two rather than seventy; the number may echo the nations listed in Genesis 10, numbered seventy in Hebrew and seventy-two in the Greek version. The road from Jerusalem down to Jericho drops steeply through lonely, rocky country known for robbers.

customs.note: Both served at the temple. Touching a corpse made a priest unclean (Leviticus 21:1), which may be part of why they passed by.
The posture of a student with a teacher (compare Acts 22:3). Mary takes a learner's place usually filled by men.

watchFor: The lawyer asks 'who is my neighbour?'; Jesus asks who acted as one (vv. 29, 36).
The hero is a Samaritan, the least expected person.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Satan
people.summary: Adversary; accuser. When used as a proper name, the Hebrew word so rendered has the article “the adversary” (Job 1:6-12; 2:1-7).

people.name: Martha
people.summary: Bitterness, the sister of Lazarus and Mary, and probably the eldest of the family, who all resided at Bethany (Luke 10:38, 40, 41; John 11:1-39).

people.name: Mary
people.summary: Mary the sister of Lazarus is brought to our notice in connection with the visits of our Lord to Bethany. She is contrasted with her sister Martha, who was “cumbered about many things” while Jesus was their guest, while Mary had chosen “the good part.”

places.name: Sodom
places.summary: Burning; the walled, a city in the vale of Siddim (Gen. 13:10; 14:1-16). The wickedness of its inhabitants brought down upon it fire from heaven, by which it was destroyed (18:16-33; 19:1-29; Deut. 23:17).

places.name: Bethsaida
places.summary: A city near which Christ fed 5,000 (Luke 9:10; comp. John 6:17; Matt. 14:15-21), and where the blind man had his sight restored (Mark 8:22), on the east side of the lake, two miles up the Jordan.

places.name: Chorazin
places.summary: Named along with Bethsaida and Capernaum as one of the cities in which our Lord’s “mighty works” were done, and which was doomed to woe because of signal privileges neglected (Matt. 11:21; Luke 10:13).

places.name: Sidon
places.summary: A fishery, a town on the Mediterranean coast, about 25 miles north of Tyre. It received its name from the “first-born” of Canaan, the grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:15, 19).

places.name: Tyre
places.summary: A rock, now es-Sur; an ancient Phoenician city, about 23 miles, in a direct line, north of Acre, and 20 south of Sidon. Sidon was the oldest Phoenician city, but Tyre had a longer and more illustrious history.

places.name: Capernaum
places.summary: Nahum’s town, a Galilean city frequently mentioned in the history of our Lord. It is not mentioned in the Old Testament. After our Lord’s expulsion from Nazareth (Matt. 4:13-16; Luke 4:16-31), Capernaum became his “own city.”

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites (Josh. 3:16).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

events.title: Good Samaritan Parable Taught
events.summary: Passage: Luke 10:25–37. People: Jesus. Place: Judea.

events.title: Jesus meets Martha and Mary
events.summary: Passage: Luke 10:38–42. People: Jesus, Martha, Mary. Place: Bethany.
